AppConfig.description:
One runnable app. `base_port` and `launch` are required; `path` is required
too whenever `defaults.doppler_yaml` cannot infer the directory.

```toml
[apps.api]
base_port    = 9100
launch       = ["doppler", "run", "-c", "dev_local", "--", "nitro", "dev", "--port", "{{ port }}"]
url_env      = "API_BASE_URL"
provides_url = true
static_env   = { SOME_JWT_SECRET = "local-dev-placeholder-value" }

[apps.web]
base_port = 4100
path      = "apps/web"
launch    = ["next", "dev", "-p", "{{ port }}"]
url_env   = "API_BASE_URL"
```

`web` names the provider through `url_env` rather than by port, so the two
apps stay wired together in every worktree.

A per-app memory cap the daemon does not enforce is the runtime's own:
`static_env = { NODE_OPTIONS = "--max-old-space-size=2048" }`, or a
`ulimit -v` wrapper in `launch`. The runtime aborts on breach and the
crash path respawns it. `[daemon] memory_max_mb` is the kernel-enforced
alternative on Linux.

base_port.description:
Start of the app's port band. Each worktree is allocated its own port
from here by the registry, so two worktrees never collide.

launch.description:
The complete launch command as one argv, run verbatim. devkit builds no
prefix of its own, so any `doppler run -c <config> --` wrapper belongs
here, and a Doppler launch whose config resolves to `prd` (or cannot be
resolved) is refused. The config comes from `-c`/`--config` here, then
`DOPPLER_CONFIG` in the app's env, then
`doppler configure get config --scope <app dir>`. Rendered as strict
minijinja over `{{ port }}`, `ports['<app>']` and
`[templates.variables]`. `ports['<app>']` is that app's port in this
worktree; when it is not running, devkit writes a pid-less reservation
that a later `devrun up <app>` claims, so a consumer can bake the port
first. A misspelled app name is an error, and a leftover `{port}` fails
the launch.

path.description:
App subdirectory relative to the repo root, when it differs from the
app's own name. Required unless `defaults.doppler_yaml` infers it, and
wins over the inferred path when set.

prep_files.description:
Files written into the app's directory during `issue setup`, before
`setup` runs. A deeper layer's list replaces this one whole.

provides_url.description:
This app serves the URL that consumer apps wire to via their `url_env`.
Exactly one app should be marked. `devrun up` of a consumer brings the
provider up too.

setup.description:
Commands run in the app's directory during `issue setup`, in order. Each
inner array is one argv (program + args), e.g.
`[["doppler","run","-c","local","--","bun","install"]]`.

static_env.description:
Env vars always set for this app, rendered as minijinja over the same
variables as `launch`. The lowest layer: a task's `env` and the CLI's
`--env` both win over it.

url.description:
Address the app serves on, as a template over the same variables as
`launch`. Defaults to `http://localhost:{{ port }}`; set it for https, a
custom host, or a path prefix. It is what `devrun up` prints and what
the provider wires into consumers. devkit never terminates TLS, and
readiness stays a TCP probe of the port.

url_env.description: Env var this app receives the `provides_url` app's URL through.

AppMatch.description:
`[harness.app_match]`: how the guard turns a hint into an app name.

Exact-name, exact-path and path-under-path matching are unconditional and
take no configuration. This table tunes only the fuzzy rung that runs when
none of those resolve, which is the one place the guard guesses.

`#[serde(default)]` sits on the container so a layer naming one key inherits
the other two rather than zeroing them.

```toml
[harness.app_match]
fuzzy     = false   # name no app rather than guess one
min_score = 75
```

fuzzy.description:
Run the fuzzy matcher at all. `false` stops after exact and path
matching, so an unrecognised hint names no app and the guard falls back
to `devkit config apps`.

max_typos.description:
Substitutions, insertions and deletions the matcher forgives.

One is what separates `lab-tools` from an app declared `lab_tools`.
`frizbee::Config::default()` allows zero, which filters exactly that
case, so this default is devkit's rather than the library's. Raising it
buys confidently wrong app names.

min_score.description:
Below this score no app is named. Pointing an agent at another app's
server is worse than naming none.

BriefConfig.description:
What `devkit brief` emits. All default on: the hooks ship enabled and
config decides whether they produce anything, so turning the output off is
one line rather than a hook-wiring task. A section with nothing to report
is omitted whatever its switch says; a switch turned off suppresses the
section, and its bullets, even when the checkout has something to put in
it. The brief's intro names only the sections that survive. Personal
defaults belong in `~/.config/devkit/config.toml`, overridden per project.

```toml
[brief]
locks = false
pins  = false
```

apps.description:
The apps section and the `devrun up` bullet. With it off, app tasks
join the task list. Live servers this worktree holds are reported
regardless: a bound port is a fact about the machine, not a listing the
brief chose to carry.

enabled.description:
The whole brief, read before any work is done. A malformed `[brief]`
table falls back to the defaults rather than withholding the brief.

locks.description:
The lock lines: the lock-enforcement sentence, or the `lockm` line when
writes are not enforced. Whether sessions ever share this checkout is
not something devkit can observe, so it is a switch rather than a probe.

rules.description:
The rules section: which of a file's rules reach the session on their
own and how to list the rest. It appears only while `[rules]` is
enabled and its source has rules to read.

tasks.description:
The task list, the task names on app lines, and the `devrun task`
bullets.

CommandRule.description:
One `[harness.commands.<name>]` entry: a set of programs whose invocation
the guard refuses, and the correction it offers instead.

Deliberately not a regex. Parsing the command, unwrapping wrappers and
runners, and removing a program's own global options (`git -C`) are
devkit's job; a rule that had to restate them would get them wrong. A rule
sees nested commands (`bash -c '...'`, `subprocess.run([...])`) and ignores
quoted text that only mentions the program.

```toml
[harness.commands.git-worktree]
programs = ["git"]
args     = ["worktree", "add"]
reason   = "use `issue setup <id>`, which records the worktree"

[harness.commands.nitro-dev]
programs = ["bun", "node"]
args     = ["**", "*nitro", "dev"] # bun --cwd . nitro dev, node node_modules/.bin/nitro dev
reason   = "start the api with `devrun up api`"
```

`args` matches the typed arguments after the program's own global options
are removed, so `git -C /repo worktree add` fires the first rule and
`git worktree list` does not. In the second rule, `**` skips any flags
before the server and `*nitro` matches the binary at any path, so it
refuses `bun --filter=api nitro dev` and allows `bun nitro build`.

action.description:
`block` refuses the command; `warn` allows it and shows the reason. A
rule whose arguments cannot be resolved (`git "$verb" add`) warns.

args.description:
Arguments that must appear, in order, at the head of the typed
arguments for the rule to fire. Empty matches any arguments. `*`
matches any run of characters, `/` included, within one argument; an
entry that is exactly `"**"` matches zero or more whole arguments. A
leading `"**"` also skips a script path, so `["**", "*nitro", "dev"]`
fires on `node server.js --name nitro dev` too.

enabled.description: `false` turns off a rule a parent layer declared.

programs.description:
Program names this rule refuses, matched against the segment's command
word by basename, and against each wrapper unwrapped to reach it
(`sudo`, `nohup`, `env`), whose own options are then its arguments. An
empty list matches nothing, which is how a child layer exempts a
subtree from a rule its parent declared.

reason.description:
Shown to the agent verbatim when the rule denies. Name the replacement
command; the agent retries from this text.

severity.description: How the message is classified for the agent.

ContextConfig.description:
Files injected into an agent's context when the condition on them holds.

```toml
[[context.files]]
path = "crates/devkit-ports/AGENTS.md"

[[context.files]]
path = "docs/deploy.md"
when = { harness = ["codex"], env = { DEPLOY_TARGET = "staging" } }
```

An entry is an array element, so a deeper `devkit.toml` replaces the whole
list rather than appending to it, the same as `[hooks]`. Repeat the
parent's entries you still want.

ContextFile.description:
One injected file. It fires once per session and counts against
`[rules] per_event_limit`. A missing file, a directory, non-UTF-8 content,
or a file over `[rules] max_file_bytes` is skipped.

path.description:
The file to inject, relative to the directory of the `devkit.toml` that
declared it.

when.description:
When to inject it. Absent means: when the edited target is under this
file's own directory.

body.description:
The minijinja source. Rendering is strict: a variable nothing supplies
is an error, and a trailing newline is kept.

description.description:
What the template is for, shown by `devkit template list` so a caller
can pick the right one.

DaemonConfig.description:
The `devkitd` supervisor: whether it starts, how long it lingers, and the
crash-loop, memory, and health policies it applies to supervised servers.

```toml
[daemon]
enabled         = true
memory_warn_mb  = 1024
memory_limit_mb = 2048   # soft: SIGTERM, then the crash path respawns
memory_action   = "restart"
memory_max_mb   = 4096   # hard: the kernel OOM-kills the tree
```

The ordering in that example is the one to keep: the soft action is the
graceful first responder, and the kernel cap is the backstop for a spike
too fast for the poll loop.

enabled.description:
Run gate: autostart the daemon only when true, `DEVKIT_DAEMON=1` is
set, or `--supervise` is passed.

health_fail_threshold.description:
Consecutive probe failures, after the server first answers, before it
is judged hung. Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_HEALTH_FAIL_THRESHOLD`.

health_probe_secs.description:
Health-probe interval in seconds; 0 disables probing (no probe thread).
A server judged hung is SIGTERMed and respawned through the crash path.
Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_HEALTH_PROBE_SECS`.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
Exit after this many idle seconds with zero clients AND zero supervised
children. Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_IDLE_SECS`.

max_restarts.description:
Crash-loop guard: restarts allowed within `restart_window_secs`. Every
restart path (crash, health probe, memory) spends this one budget.
Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_MAX_RESTARTS`.

memory_action.description:
Action when tree-RSS crosses `memory_limit_mb`: "warn" (log a line) or
"restart" (SIGTERM and let the crash path respawn). Any other value
falls back to warn. Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_MEMORY_ACTION`.

memory_limit_mb.description:
Take `memory_action` past this tree-RSS in MB (0 = off). A restart needs
`memory_action = "restart"`. Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_MEM_LIMIT_MB`.

memory_limit_ticks.description:
Consecutive supervision ticks at or over `memory_limit_mb` before the
restart action fires (debounces transient allocation spikes). A tick
is 500 ms.
Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_MEM_LIMIT_TICKS`.

memory_max_mb.description:
Hard kernel memory ceiling per supervised tree, in MB (0 = off,
Linux-only). A breach OOM-kills the tree and the crash path respawns it.
Set above memory_limit_mb. Needs a delegated cgroup-v2 subtree, which
`devkitd install-service` sets up; without one it warns once and falls
back to the soft action. Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_MEM_MAX_MB`.

memory_warn_mb.description:
Log a loud line past this supervised tree-RSS in MB (0 = off). Warns
only; it restarts nothing. Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_MEM_WARN_MB`.

restart_window_secs.description:
Length of the sliding window the `max_restarts` budget is counted over.
Env: `DEVKIT_DAEMON_RESTART_WINDOW`.

Defaults.description:
Project-wide paths and branch conventions. Each key is independently
optional and empty (or, for `apps_dir`/`pr_base`/`stray_scan_width`, its own
documented default) when unset; an empty path or branch key is not
validated at config load, and what happens when it is used is up to the
feature that reads it.

`worktree_root`, `baseline_dir` and `doppler_yaml` resolve once, when the
config loads. `${VAR}` becomes that environment variable, and an unset one
is an error naming the key and the variable; `$$` is a literal `$`, and a
`$` followed by anything else is left alone. A leading `~/` then becomes
`$HOME`. A path still relative anchors to what its key names, never to the
working directory, and `.` and `..` fold out. `branch_prefix` gets the
`${VAR}` step only.

`worktree_root` and `baseline_dir` anchor to the layer that declared them,
so a project can commit this table as it stands and have it hold on every
machine:

```toml
[defaults]
worktree_root = "../myproject_worktrees"
baseline_dir  = "../myproject_worktrees/_baselines"
baseline_ref  = "origin/main"
```

Only `branch_prefix` is personal. Put it in `devkit.local.toml`, or write
`"${USER}/"`.

apps_dir.description:
Repo-relative directory apps live under (e.g. "apps"). Used to infer app
paths from doppler.yaml and to detect changed apps in a diff.

baseline_dir.description:
Directory baseline worktrees are created under, one per fork-point
commit, each made on demand. Anchors like `worktree_root`. Defaults to
`_baselines` under `worktree_root`. `devrun baseline prune` reclaims
only directories carrying devkit's `.devkit/baseline.toml` marker, and
only once no worktree's `.devkit/issue.toml` names them. A directory
here without that marker is reported and never touched. A baseline
devkit expects whose marker is missing is rebuilt in place, and one
whose marker cannot be read is refused.

baseline_ref.description:
Git ref the baseline server tracks, e.g. `origin/staging`. Defaults to
the remote's default branch from `origin/HEAD`; when neither resolves,
set this or run `git remote set-head origin -a`.

branch_prefix.description:
Prefix on branches created by `issue setup`, e.g. `you/`. `${VAR}`
expands, as in `"${USER}/"`, and nothing else does.

doppler_yaml.description:
Path to the repo's `doppler.yaml`; its `setup` paths seed app path
inference. Names a file inside the repository, so a relative value
anchors to the checkout reading the config: each worktree resolves its
own copy. Leave empty and every app needs its own `path`.

ignored_checks.description:
Glob patterns for status-check names to discount from a PR's CHECK
verdict — e.g. a deploy left red by an unfinished PR. Matched
case-insensitively against each check's name; a PR reads green when only
ignored checks fail, and the ignored failures are still surfaced in the
triage output rather than hidden.

issue_summary.description:
Write the issue summary file on every `issue setup`, as though
`--summary` were passed. `--summary` / `--no-summary` still win for one
run. Its path and body come from `templates.issue_summary_path` and
`templates.issue_summary`.

pr_base.description:
Base branch `issue pr create` opens PRs against (e.g. "main",
"staging"). `--base` overrides it for one run.

pr_create_state.description:
State `issue pr create` opens a PR in when neither `--draft` nor
`--ready` is given. Draft by default, so a new PR never lands in
anyone's review queue until it is marked ready.

pr_proof_variable.description:
The `[templates.variables]` name whose `--arg` carries a PR's proof.
When set, an agent's `issue pr create` in an issue worktree is refused
before the push unless that proof answers every item of the issue's
`Done when` or `Acceptance criteria` section, each on a line starting
with the item's number (`2. <evidence>`). Unset by default.

require_pr_reviewer.description:
Refuse any run that would leave a PR ready for review with no human
GitHub reviewer other than its own author: `issue pr create --ready`,
`issue pr ready`, and the draft-to-ready flip in `issue review request`.
Off by default.

stray_scan_width.description:
Width of each app's port-band scan window for stray detection:
ports `[base_port, base_port + stray_scan_width)`. Default 64.

worktree_include.description:
Glob patterns (relative to the primary checkout's root) for untracked
local files `issue setup` and `issue pr checkout` copy into a new
worktree, and `issue sync-includes` into existing ones. Existing
destinations are left alone, and a failed copy warns. Anchor patterns
(`apps/*/.env.local`): `**` descends into `node_modules`. `a/**` matches
every path below `a`, direct children included; a bare `**` covers the
checkout root. A directory match or a trailing `/` copies recursively,
reading the whole subtree into memory first.

A symlink is reproduced as a link to the same target; on Windows that
needs Developer Mode or administrator rights, and a refused link warns
and is skipped. A symlinked directory that is a pattern's own anchor
(`linked/**`) is walked through; write `linked/` to get the link.

worktree_root.description:
Directory issue worktrees are created under. Names a location on this
machine, so a relative value anchors to the directory of the config
layer that declared it, even when that layer is the repository's main
checkout. Defaults to the primary checkout's `_worktrees` sibling, e.g.
`~/git/example_worktrees` beside `~/git/example`.

DocsManifest.description:
Libraries whose source is checked out at the version this project resolves.
A project's `[docs]` section overlays the global `docs.toml` entry by entry.

```toml
[[docs.libs]]
name  = "minijinja"
notes = "template syntax for [tasks] and [templates]"

[[docs.libs]]
name      = "node-types"
ecosystem = "js"
package   = "@types/node"
```

The first entry names nothing but the library, so its ecosystem and version
both come from the project's own lockfiles. The second overrides the
registry name, which is the only thing `name` cannot also serve as.

libs.description:
One entry per managed library. Every field except `name` is optional so
an overlay can override a single field of a global entry.

Ecosystem.description:
Which importer graph resolves a library's version, and therefore which
lockfile is consulted.

oneOf.description: No package registry or lockfile; pinned by `ref` or default branch.

EventTransition.description: A status move: from any status in `from` to `to`.

from.description:
The statuses the issue may move from. `*` matches any status, and the
empty string matches an issue with no status (on GitHub, one outside
`[github] project` or with the field unset). Names match
case-insensitively, ignoring surrounding whitespace. `["*"]` when
unset.

to.description:
The status the issue moves to, matched like `from`. An issue already
there is left alone, whatever `from` says.

Fidelity.description:
What a logged command carries. Ordered least to most revealing, so
resolving across config layers is `min` and no layer can raise it.

oneOf.description: A stable digest and nothing else.
The text, with known token shapes substituted by kind.
The text verbatim.

FileCondition.description: Conditions on an injected file. Every condition present must hold.

env.description:
Environment variables in the hook process. An empty value means
"present with any value".

path.description: A glob over the repo-relative targets of the tool call.

ForgeConfig.description:
Where this project's pull requests live. Absent means detect from the
`origin` host: github.com, gitlab.com and codeberg.org, else no forge.

```toml
[forge]
kind = "gitlab"
host = "gitlab.example.com"
repo = "platform/app"
```

host.description:
The forge's hostname, for a self-hosted instance such as GitHub
Enterprise Server or a company GitLab. Defaults to the kind's public
host: github.com, gitlab.com, or codeberg.org. Needs `kind`.

kind.description:
Force a forge instead of detecting one. With no forge, commands that
read or write a pull request fail and say so; worktrees, ports, locks
and docs keep working. `none` declares that this project has no pull
requests, so `issue end` finishes a worktree once its tracker issue is
done, its tree is clean and its commits are on a remote. Detection that
finds no forge holds that verdict open instead, because `issue end`
deletes branches. `devkit doctor`'s `forge` row shows which forge
resolved and why.

repo.description:
Repository pull requests are opened against, e.g. `upstream/app`, or
`group/subgroup/app` on GitLab. Defaults from an `origin` remote on the
forge's host (an ssh alias is resolved with `ssh -G`). `issue prs
--repo` overrides it for one run, and an ambient `GH_REPO` never does.

ForgeKind.description: A git forge devkit's PR commands can talk to.

oneOf.description: github.com, or GitHub Enterprise Server through `host`.
gitlab.com, or a self-managed GitLab through `host`.
Forgejo or Gitea. codeberg.org unless `host` names another instance.

GithubConfig.description:
Which GitHub repository holds this project's issues, for the GitHub
tracker, and which Projects v2 project holds their status for
`[issue.events]`. The repository pull requests go to is `[forge] repo`,
since a project on any forge has one.

Unknown keys are refused: a misspelled `issue_repo` ignored would default
from `origin` and query another repository's issues.

```toml
[github]
issues_repo = "org/planning"
project = "org/3"
status_field = "Status"
```

issues_repo.description:
Repository holding the issues, e.g. `org/planning`. Defaults from an
`origin` remote on the GitHub host the forge names (github.com unless
`[forge] host` says otherwise; an ssh alias is resolved with
`ssh -G`); otherwise the error names this key.

no_graphql.description:
Skip GitHub's GraphQL API. A call with a REST path goes straight to
it, one request per item where GraphQL would batch them; one with
none, such as `issue prs`, fails naming this key. Unset, devkit tries
GraphQL first and uses REST only where GitHub refuses GraphQL outright.
`DEVKIT_NO_GRAPHQL` (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` or `0`/`false`/`no`/`off`)
wins over this.

project.description:
The Projects v2 project whose single-select field holds the issues'
status, which `[issue.events]` moves under the GitHub tracker:
`"owner/N"`, or a bare `N` owned by `issues_repo`'s owner. Without it,
a GitHub tracker's events fail naming this key.

status_field.description:
The single-select field on `project` that holds the status. `Status`
when unset.

HarnessSection.description:
The `[harness]` table of a checkout's `devkit.toml`.

This is the shape `devkit schema` renders. Nothing at runtime deserializes
the table through it: the probe reads each key independently so one bad key
cannot take the others down with it, which also means a misspelled key
changes nothing and reports nothing.

`enforce_writes` and `enforce_commands` are on if any layer sets them.
`shell` and the three policy keys take the closest layer's value. A
checkout opting in is read for its `[harness]` table alone, so its
`devkit.toml` may hold nothing else.

```toml
[harness]
enforce_writes   = true
enforce_commands = true
script_files     = "warn"
```

The same two lines in `~/.config/devkit/config.toml` enforce across every
checkout, with no per-project file at all.

app_match.description:
How the guard resolves a guarded command to one of `[apps]`, from a
workspace path in the command, a `--filter`/`--dir`/`-C` value, or the
shell's directory.

commands.description:
Extra refusals beyond the ones devkit derives from `[apps]` and
`[tasks]`. Merged across config layers by name; redefining a rule
overrides only the keys it sets.

enforce_commands.description:
Refuse shell commands devkit already has a wired-up path for: a
`[harness.commands]` rule, a retyped task, an app's launch, or a known
dev server. devkit's own binaries always run. Fails open.
`DEVKIT_ENFORCE_COMMANDS` overrides it.

enforce_writes.description:
Claim a lock on every file an agent's edit or resolvable shell write
touches, and deny a write another session holds. Resolves per
checkout, first answer wins: `DEVKIT_ENFORCE_WRITES` (`1`/`true`/`yes`/
`on` or `0`/`false`/`no`/`off`; anything else falls through), then any
project layer for the written path (`devkit.local.toml` and a linked
worktree's main-checkout layer included), then the global config. A
project layer that does not parse is skipped, so it cannot switch off
another layer's opt-in. Fails closed on a registry error.

issue_tools.description:
MCP tools that create or edit issues, whose title and body must come
from `devkit issue render`. Merged across config layers by name.
Enforces on its own presence, independent of `enforce_commands`.

log.description: What devkit records about the events a harness sends it.

pr_tools.description:
MCP tools that open or edit PRs, whose title and body must come from
`devkit issue pr render`. Merged across config layers by name.
Enforces on its own presence, independent of `enforce_commands`.

script_files.description:
A call to a stored script (`python3 tools/gen.py`), whose contents are
not read.

shell.description: The shell a hook command is read in.

unresolved_writes.description:
A write, or code that may write, whose target could not be determined.
Claiming some other path never covers it.

unsupported_language.description:
Executable source in a language devkit cannot analyze, such as
`perl -e` or `ruby -e`. An `awk` program counts only when it could
write.

HoldStop.description: Whose stop `[todo] hold_stop` refuses while the agent has open todos.

oneOf.description: Every agent's stop, a main agent's included.
Only a sub-agent's stop.
No stop.

HoldStopSpelling.description: What `[todo] hold_stop` accepts: a mode, or a boolean.

HooksConfig.description:
Commands run on a devkit lifecycle event. Most keys are named
`{before,after}_<event>` after the state change rather than the command
that reached it; `after_end` is the exception and names its run, because a
run-level event has exactly one caller and no worktree state to be named
for. Each key holds a list of argv arrays — no shell, so pipes, `&&`, and
globs are not available. A hook that fails to render, spawn, or exit zero
warns on stderr and the remaining hooks still run. Output is captured and
discarded. A `devkit.toml` that fails to load leaves `issue end` with no
hooks, so none of its keys run.

```toml
[hooks]
after_worktree_create = [["zoxide", "add", "{{ worktree }}"]]
after_worktree_remove = [["zoxide", "remove", "{{ worktree }}"]]
after_end             = [["alacritree", "project", "refresh"]]
```

Each key is an array, so a deeper `devkit.toml` replaces the whole list
rather than appending to it. A project defining a key drops the
machine-wide list from `~/.config/devkit/config.toml` entirely.

after_end.description:
Runs once at the end of an `issue end` run that removed at least one
worktree, after every `after_worktree_remove` hook, in the main
repository root. It carries `removed` (the removed paths, in confirmed
order, rendered as one argv slot), `count`, `prefix`, `worktree_root`,
`primary`, and `[templates.variables]`, and none of the single-worktree
keys. Skipped with a warning, like `after_worktree_remove`, when the
main repository root does not resolve.

after_worktree_create.description:
Runs once in the root of a worktree `issue setup` or
`issue pr checkout` has just created, after its apps are prepared and
after the command has reported the worktree. Each argv element is
rendered as minijinja over `worktree`, `branch`, `issue`, `slug`,
`apps`, `prefix`, `role`, and `[templates.variables]`. Output is
discarded, so the command's JSON stays the last line on stdout.

after_worktree_remove.description:
Runs once per worktree `issue end` removed, after every removal in the
run has finished, in the main repository root. `issue`, `slug` and
`apps` come from the `.devkit/issue.toml` record read before the
removal. Rendered over `worktree`, `branch`, `issue`, `slug`, `apps`,
`prefix`, `worktree_root`, `primary`, and `[templates.variables]`. A
worktree kept back or skipped fires nothing. Runs after the run's
summary, so a failing hook never un-reports a removal, and is skipped
with a warning when the main repository root does not resolve.

before_worktree_remove.description:
Runs once in the root of each worktree `issue end` is about to remove,
after `[preserve]` has copied its files out and before any removal in
the run starts. Worktrees run one at a time, in confirmed order.
Rendered over the same keys as `after_worktree_remove`. A failing hook
warns and the worktree is still removed. A worktree kept back or
skipped fires nothing.

IssueConfig.description:
The `[issue]` table. Each event moves the issue's status (a Linear state,
or `[github] status_field`) from a `from` status to `to`; an event with no
table does nothing. The statuses name one board, so keep the events in the
repository's `devkit.toml`: tables merge key by key across layers.

```toml
[issue.events.setup]
to = "Todo"

[issue.events.start]
from = ["", "Todo", "Backlog"]
to = "In progress"

[issue.events.pr_open]
to = "In review"

[github]
project = 3            # or "some-org/7"
status_field = "Status"
```

events.description:
Status moves, keyed by the event that fires them. The event names are
fixed, so a misspelled one is a parse error.

IssueEventsConfig.description: One optional status move per event.

pr_open.description:
Fired by `issue pr create`, whether it opened the PR or found one open.
A failed move warns and the PR stays as it is.

setup.description:
Fired by `issue setup` as its last step, after the
`after_worktree_create` hooks. A failed move warns and setup succeeds.

start.description:
Fired by the first agent session in a worktree `issue setup` created,
once per worktree, in the background. `issue pr checkout` worktrees
never fire it. List the states work starts from in `from`: `["*"]` lets
a second worktree pull an issue back from review.

LayerMarker.description:
The `[config]` table. Read straight off the raw layer by `is_root_layer`
rather than through `Config`, because it decides which layers exist before
there is a merged config to deserialize; this type exists so the published
JSON Schema can still describe it.

```toml
[config]
root = true
```

root.description:
Stop walking upward at this file, and drop
`~/.config/devkit/config.toml` from the layer stack, all but its
`[todo]` table, which describes the machine rather than a project.

LibEntry.description:
One managed library. Every field except `name` is optional so a project
overlay entry can override a single field of a global entry.

docs_dir.description: Docs directory inside the checkout, overriding layout detection.

ecosystem.description:
Which importer graph resolves the version. Omit to detect it from the
project's lockfiles.

exclude.description:
Gitignore-style patterns every checkout leaves out, neither downloaded
nor written (e.g. `["testdata/", "*.json"]`). Global manifest only: a
checkout is shared by every project, so a project layer that set its
own list would rewrite the tree under the others.

name.description:
Id this library is addressed by on the `docm` command line, and the
key an overlay entry merges onto.

notes.description:
Freeform note surfaced by `docm info` and `docm list`: what this
library is here for.

package.description: Registry package name when it differs from `name` (e.g. `@types/node`).

ref.description: Manual pin (tag/branch/sha); wins over lockfile resolution.

repo.description: Git URL to clone, skipping the registry lookup that would find it.

src_dir.description: Source directory inside the checkout, overriding layout detection.

LinearConfig.description:
Linear lookups that cost an extra API round trip, so each is opt-in.

```toml
[linear]
resolve_pr_links = true
```

The lookup authenticates with `LINEAR_API_KEY` from the environment or
`~/.config/devkit/secrets.toml`; no token lives in this table.

resolve_pr_links.description:
Query Linear for the issues linked to each PR in `issue prs` and the
`issue.prs` MCP action, adding every linked id to the ISSUE column. One
extra batched round trip per 25 PRs. Fail-soft: with no key or on a
Linear error the column keeps the id derived from the PR text. Linear
only; under the GitHub tracker the column carries each PR's closing
issues regardless.

LogSection.description:
Harness logging: what agents tried to run, and what devkit decided about
it. Off unless the global config turns it on. `devkit doctor`'s
`harness_log` row shows the mode in force.

`enabled = true`, `dir`, `auto_prune`, `max_age_days` and `max_bytes` are
read from `~/.config/devkit/config.toml` alone and ignored wherever else
they appear. A project layer may do exactly two things: set
`enabled = false`, and lower `command` or `prompt`. Everything a project
layer can do tightens. `dir` is on that list for the same reason
`enabled = true` is: a project layer setting `dir = "./.logs"` would land
command text inside the checkout. That boundary guards against a
`devkit.toml` a project ships, not against your own environment:
`$DEVKIT_CONFIG` can point anywhere, a repository included.

```toml
[harness.log]
enabled      = true              # global config only
command      = "redacted"        # full | redacted | hashed
prompt       = "off"             # off | hashed | redacted | full
auto_prune   = true              # global config only
dir          = "${HOME}/logs/devkit" # global only; defaults under state_dir
max_age_days = 30                # global only; absent means unlimited
max_bytes    = 2000000000        # global only; absent means unlimited
```

Every leaf is `Option` so a layer that set nothing is distinguishable from
one that set the default, which is what the downward clamp needs.

auto_prune.description: Sweep the log directory at session end. Global config only.

command.description:
How much of a command's text a record carries, `redacted` by default.
Resolves to the lowest value any layer sets, so no project can raise
it. Redaction is best effort: it replaces `LINEAR_API_KEY`,
`LINEAR_WORKSPACE`, `SLACK_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` and those
services' token prefixes with a placeholder naming the kind. It misses
novel formats, credentials under other names, and anything read from a
file, so a `redacted` log is not safe to share on that basis alone.

dir.description: Where records land. Global config only; defaults under the state dir.

enabled.description:
Turn logging on. Read from the global config alone; a project layer
may only set it false. `DEVKIT_HARNESS_LOG` wins over both.

max_age_days.description:
Days of records to keep. Global config only; absent means unlimited,
and `0` is rejected as ambiguous.

max_bytes.description:
Bytes of records to keep. Global config only; absent means unlimited,
and `0` is rejected as ambiguous.

prompt.description:
How much of a submitted prompt a record carries, `off` by default.
Resolves to the lowest value any layer sets.

McpConfig.description:
The `devkit-mcp` server. The plugins register it unconditionally and a
harness may re-enable a server the user switched off, so config is where
it stays off.

```toml
[mcp]
enabled = false
```

enabled.description:
Whether the server offers its tools. Off, it still answers the
handshake but lists no tools and refuses every call. Read once at
startup from the directory the harness started it in, so a change lands
on the next session or reconnect. A config that fails to load leaves it
on.

ParallelismConfig.description:
Width of the shared worker pool. Machine tuning rather than a project
convention, so it belongs in the personal layer at
`~/.config/devkit/config.toml` rather than a repository's `devkit.toml`.

```toml
[parallelism]
threads = 8
```

threads.description:
Threads in the pool devkit shares across its parallel work, 4 when
unset. `DEVKIT_THREADS` wins over this; an unparseable or zero value
there is ignored. Zero is refused here rather than clamped, because
rayon reads a zero thread count as one thread per core. Raising it
helps most where a stat is slow, such as a Windows drive under WSL.

Person.description:
A team member's handle mapping (Slack user-id, GitHub login, etc.). No
token lives here: `SLACK_TOKEN` resolves from the environment or
`~/.config/devkit/secrets.toml`.

```toml
[people.alice]
slack  = "U0XXXXXXXXX"
github = "alice-gh"
```

github.description:
GitHub login requested as the PR reviewer when this alias is passed to
`issue review request --to`. Omit and the alias only gets Slacked.

slack.description: Slack user or channel id, e.g. `U0XXXXXXXXX`.

PolicyAction.description:
What a policy finding does to the tool call. A warning never overrides a
lock conflict on a target devkit did resolve.

oneOf.description: Deny the tool call with an actionable reason.
Allow it and tell the agent what was not checked.
Allow it silently.

PostgresConfig.description:
Where `[todo] backend = "postgres"` finds its database: the connection
URL `DEVKIT_TODO_DATABASE_URL` resolves to, from the environment, then
this Doppler scope when set, then the secrets file.

```toml
[todo.postgres]
root = "factory"
```

ca_file.description:
A PEM file of CA certificates to trust, besides the bundled and
platform roots, when verifying the database's certificate. Supabase
signs its certificates with its own CA, which its dashboard offers
for download. Read from `~/.config/devkit/config.toml` (or
`$DEVKIT_CONFIG`) alone and ignored in a project's `devkit.toml`, so
a checkout cannot add a CA your connection trusts.

doppler_config.description: The Doppler config to read it from. Doppler's own default when absent.

doppler_project.description:
Read the connection URL, when the environment lacks it, from this
Doppler project, before the secrets file. Hooks reuse the URL Doppler
last gave, kept in devkit's state directory, until it ages out or
fails to connect.

root.description:
The database tenant containing this workflow's todos and activity.
Defaults to `devkit`. This is independent of node templates.

PrCreateState.description:
The state a PR is opened in by `issue pr create` when neither `--draft` nor
`--ready` is passed.

oneOf.description: Opened as a draft. Reviewers are notified only once it is marked ready.
Opened ready for review.

PrepFile.description:
A file written into an app's directory during `issue setup`, before the
app's `setup` commands run. Parent directories are created. Existing files
are left untouched unless `overwrite` is set.

```toml
[apps.web]
base_port = 4100
launch    = ["next", "dev", "-p", "{{ port }}"]

[[apps.web.prep_files]]
path    = ".env.local"
content = """
SOME_FEATURE_FLAG=dummy
"""
```

content.description:
File contents, rendered as minijinja over `prefix`, `issue`, `slug`,
`apps`, `app`, `branch`, `worktree`, `role` and `[templates.variables]`,
then written with no newline added. Emit a literal `{{` with
`{% raw %}...{% endraw %}`.

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing file rather than skipping it.

path.description: Target path, relative to the app's directory.

PreserveConfig.description:
Files copied out of a worktree before `issue end` removes it. Each entry
names its own destination, so one run can archive different files to
different places. A failure warns and the worktree goes anyway, unless the
entry is `required`. Entries run serially in sorted name order, before any
removal. Symlinks are followed, the opposite of `worktree_include`, so an
archive may outlive the link's target.

`deny_unknown_fields` because a misspelled `required` would otherwise be
consumed silently, leaving the entry fail-open while the user believes the
files are protected.

```toml
[preserve.scratch]
from     = [".scratch/"]
to       = "{{ worktree_root }}/archive/{{ issue }}/scratch"
required = true

[preserve.notes]
from = ["docs/notes/*.md"]
to   = "{{ primary }}/.devkit/archive/{{ issue }}"
```

`scratch` is `required`, so a failure there keeps the worktree, its branch
and its summary instead of removing them. `notes` warns and the worktree
goes.

from.description:
Glob patterns for the files to copy, relative to the worktree root and
rendered as minijinja. Name a directory (`.scratch/`) or write
`.scratch/**` to archive its whole tree; `dir/*` takes direct children
only. A pattern that could reach outside the worktree (absolute, rooted,
holding `..`, or drive-relative like `C:scratch`) is skipped with a
warning; one that matches nothing is not a failure. The default issue
summary sits under the worktree's `.devkit/`, where a pattern such as
`.devkit/ISSUE_SUMMARY_*.md` reaches it; a relative
`templates.issue_summary_path` puts it outside, where no pattern does.

required.description:
Keep the worktree, its branch and its summary when this entry warns,
and exit non-zero. Governs errors only, never an empty match.

to.description:
Destination directory, rendered as minijinja over `worktree`, `branch`,
`issue`, `slug`, `apps`, `prefix`, `worktree_root`, `primary` and
`[templates.variables]`. Issue fields come from the worktree's
`.devkit/issue.toml` and render empty without one, and `primary` fails
when the primary checkout cannot be resolved. Must render to a
non-empty absolute path outside every worktree the run removes; the
filesystem decides that, so a symlink, `..` or case difference does not
slip past. Created when the first file lands. An existing file there is
truncated and rewritten, so an interrupted copy leaves a short file.
Two worktrees writing one filename into the same `to` collide; render
`{{ issue }}` into it.

anyOf.description: `"owner/N"`: project `N` of the user or organization `owner`.

ProjectRef.description:
A GitHub Projects v2 project: its number, and its owner when that is not
the issues repository's owner.

PromptFidelity.description:
What a logged prompt carries. Same ordering rule as [`Fidelity`], with an
`off` below every level of it: a corpus can carry full command text without
carrying what the human typed.

oneOf.description: Record that a prompt was submitted, and none of its text.

RenderedToolRule.description:
One `[harness.issue_tools.<name>]` or `[harness.pr_tools.<name>]` entry: an
MCP tool that creates or edits issues or PRs, whose title and body the
pre-tool-use hook allows only when `devkit issue render` (an issue) or
`devkit issue pr render` (a PR) produced them in the same agent session.

```toml
[harness.issue_tools.linear]
servers    = ["*linear*"]
tools      = ["save_issue"]
absent     = ["id"]
title      = "title"
body       = "description"
body_patch = ["patch"]

[harness.issue_tools.github]
servers = ["*github*"]
tools   = ["issue_write"]
equals  = { method = "create" }
title   = "title"
body    = "body"

[harness.pr_tools.github-create]
servers = ["*github*"]
tools   = ["create_pull_request"]
title   = "title"
body    = "body"

[harness.pr_tools.github-update]
servers = ["*github*"]
tools   = ["update_pull_request"]
absent  = ["pullNumber"]
title   = "title"
body    = "body"
```

absent.description:
Input keys that must be missing or null for the call to count as a
create. Any other call is an update.

body.description: The input key holding the body.

body_patch.description:
Input keys that edit the body without carrying it whole. A call
carrying one is denied, since no render can vouch for the result.

enabled.description: `false` turns off an entry a parent layer declared.

equals.description:
Input keys that must equal the given string for the call to count as a
create.

servers.description:
MCP server names this entry covers, matched case-insensitively; `*`
matches any run of characters. Empty matches any server.

title.description: The input key holding the title.

tools.description:
MCP tool names this entry covers, matched exactly. Empty matches
nothing.

Required.description:
Who must supply an `--arg` even though a default exists. `Never` is the
absence of a marking, not a licence to omit: the derived rule (an arg with
no default is required) is a floor this enum sits on top of and cannot
lower. `Never` is therefore meaningful only as a task-level override of a
variable-level marking. Who counts as an agent is `DEVKIT_CALLER`, then a
harness session variable, then a non-terminal stdin.

RoleConfig.description:
A caller's workflow role, independent of its authority over claims.

```toml
[todo.roles.manager]
scope = "workspace"
[todo.roles.implementer]
scope = "agent"
parent = "manager"
agent_types = ["implementer"]
hold_pending = true
```

agent_types.description: Subagent types assigned this role by the subagent-start hook.

hold_pending.description:
Hold a stop on pending todos at the role's node. When absent, true
only when the template includes the caller's deepest identity:
`agent` for a subagent and `session` for a main agent.

parent.description: The role it works under. Selects suggested roles, never claim authority.

scope.description: The scope this role writes to, walking up when caller facts are missing.

RuleAction.description:
What a matching command rule does. A rule that should not act is disabled
with `enabled = false`, so there is no `allow`.

RulesConfig.description:
Rule injection settings. When an agent is about to write a file, devkit
injects the rules governing it from a prebuilt JSON index.

Injection fires on the structured edits the write stage allows (`Edit`,
`Write`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`, `apply_patch`), whether or not
`[harness] enforce_writes` is on; shell writes inject nothing. Each rule
fires once per session, and compaction resets that record. Only targets
inside the repository inject. Separately, the session-start and
post-compact hooks print the repository's `must` rules through
`devkit rules context`.

```toml
[rules]
enabled = true
min_severity = "should"
per_event_limit = 5
source = "file"
```

enabled.description: Rule and file injection as a whole.

index.description:
The `file` source's index: a `repo-rules-agent` SQLite store or a
legacy JSON index, told apart by the file's contents whatever it is
called. Absent means the extractor's cache directory for this
checkout's main worktree, preferring its `index.sqlite` over its
`index.json` as the extractor does, so a built index needs no config.
`devkit rules add|edit|remove` change the same file; a SQLite store is
edited under the extractor's pinning rules, so `repo-rules index`
keeps the edits. When `devkit rules stats` reports no index, build one
or point this at it.

max_event_bytes.description: The rendered total for one event is truncated to this.

max_file_bytes.description: A single injected file larger than this is skipped.

min_severity.description: The least severe rule still injected: `must`, `should` or `can`.

per_event_limit.description: How many rules and files one event may inject.

source.description:
Where rules are read from and where `devkit rules add|edit|remove`
write: `file`, the index file at `index`; `postgres`, the repository
`rules.postgres.repository` names in `repo-rules-agent`'s shared
Postgres store; or `supabase`, the repository
`rules.supabase.repository` names in that store reached over a
Supabase project's Data API. Both remote sources are read through a
local cache that session start refreshes.

RulesPostgresConfig.description:
Where `[rules] source = "postgres"` finds its rules: the repository
`repository` names in the database whose connection URL
`DEVKIT_RULES_DATABASE_URL` resolves to, from the environment, then this
Doppler scope when set, then the secrets file. The database carries
`repo-rules-agent`'s query schema, `repo_rules`, and the connection's role
reads and edits it directly.

```toml
[rules]
source = "postgres"

[rules.postgres]
repository = "0b6f6c1e-8f0e-4a43-9d55-3c0d2b1f9a10"
doppler_project = "repo-rules"
doppler_config = "dev"
```

ca_file.description:
A PEM file of CA certificates to trust, besides the bundled and
platform roots, when verifying the database's certificate. Read from
`~/.config/devkit/config.toml` (or `$DEVKIT_CONFIG`) alone and ignored
in a project's `devkit.toml`, so a checkout cannot add a CA your
connection trusts.

doppler_config.description: The Doppler config to read it from. Doppler's own default when absent.

doppler_project.description:
Read the connection URL, when the environment lacks it, from this
Doppler project, before the secrets file. Hooks reuse the URL Doppler
last gave, kept in devkit's state directory: session start asks
Doppler again once it ages out and keeps it when Doppler gives none,
write hooks never ask Doppler, and a login the database refuses
drops it.

repository.description:
The repository's UUID in the store, its `repo_id`. The source reads
and edits that repository's rules alone.

oneOf.description:
The index file `repo-rules-agent` writes, SQLite or JSON, at
`[rules] index`.
`repo-rules-agent`'s Postgres store, at `[rules.postgres]`.

`repo-rules-agent`'s store over a Supabase project's Data API, at
`[rules.supabase]`.

RulesSupabaseConfig.description:
Where `[rules] source = "supabase"` finds its rules: the repository
`repository` names, read through `repo-rules-agent`'s `repo_rules_api`
functions on a Supabase project's Data API as a signed-in user.
`devkit auth supabase` signs in; hooks use that session, or sign in with
`DEVKIT_RULES_SUPABASE_EMAIL` and `DEVKIT_RULES_SUPABASE_PASSWORD`, which
resolve from the environment, then this Doppler scope when set, then the
secrets file.

```toml
[rules]
source = "supabase"

[rules.supabase]
url = "https://abcdefghijklmnop.supabase.co"
repository = "0b6f6c1e-8f0e-4a43-9d55-3c0d2b1f9a10"
publishable_key = "sb_publishable_example"
callback_port = 7471           # the default; the allow list needs it exactly
doppler_project = "repo-rules" # optional
doppler_config = "ci"          # optional
```

callback_port.description:
The local port `devkit auth supabase` takes the browser's sign-in
on. The project's redirect allow list must hold
`http://localhost:<callback_port>/callback` exactly.

doppler_config.description:
The Doppler config to read them from. Doppler's own default when
absent.

doppler_project.description:
Read the sign-in email and password, when the environment lacks
them, from this Doppler project, before the secrets file. Hooks reuse
what Doppler last gave, kept in devkit's state directory: session
start asks Doppler again once it ages out and keeps it when Doppler
gives none, write hooks never ask Doppler, and a sign-in the API
refuses drops it.

publishable_key.description:
The project's publishable key, sent as `apikey` with a signed-in
user's token. Without it, requests carry no credentials, for a proxy
that attaches them.

repository.description:
The repository's UUID in the store, its `repo_id`. The source reads
and edits that repository's rules alone.

url.description:
The project's API URL, `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co`. Read
from `~/.config/devkit/config.toml` (or `$DEVKIT_CONFIG`) alone and
ignored in a project's `devkit.toml`, so a checkout cannot send your
session elsewhere. `DEVKIT_RULES_SUPABASE_URL` overrides it.

anyOf.description:
Renders, then splits on `on` (never empty) into a run of separate
arguments. A template rendering empty contributes no arguments at all.
Pick an `on` the values cannot contain. Splits come last in `run`,
after at least two plain entries, or the command guard cannot recognize
the task.

RunAction.description:
A `run` entry written as a table. Each action is recognized by its own
template key, so the key sets of any two actions must stay disjoint.

`deny_unknown_fields` because actions are matched untagged: without it a
misspelled key alongside a well-formed `split`/`on` pair deserializes
silently, and the typo changes nothing the author can see.

anyOf.description: Renders to exactly one argument, whatever the result contains.
A table naming what to do with the rendered result.

RunArg.description:
One entry of a task's `run`, each rendering exactly one minijinja template
and differing only in what it does with the result.

```toml
[tasks.stage]
run = ["git", "add", "--", { split = "{{ files }}", on = ";" }]
```

`devrun task stage --arg 'files=new file.txt;other.txt'` reaches `git` as
four arguments, the space in the first filename included, because devkit
execs the argv rather than handing it to a shell.

ScopeConfig.description:
A named todo node template in the scope tree.

```toml
[todo.scopes.review]
node = "{repo}.{branch}.review-{session}"
parent = "workspace"
```

node.description:
Segments joined by dots. Placeholders are `repo`, `branch`,
`harness`, `session` and `agent`.

parent.description:
The scope to use when a caller lacks a template value. The one root
has no parent and its node contains no placeholders.

Severity.description: How a diagnostic is classified for the agent.

ShellSetting.description:
The shell whose syntax a hook command is read in. `auto` reads Claude
Code's `PowerShell` tool and Codex on Windows as PowerShell, and everything
else as bash. The hook process's own `SHELL` and `MSYSTEM` are never read.

Step.description:
One step of a sequence task: run a sibling command task, or bring an app up.

```toml
[tasks.stack]
steps = [{ task = "api-build" }, { up = "api" }]
```

oneOf.description: Name of a sibling command task to run at this point in the sequence.

Name of an app to bring up. Idempotent: an app already running in this
worktree is reported rather than spawned again.

SupabaseConfig.description:
Where `[todo] backend = "supabase"` reaches the todo database: a
Supabase project's Data API, with the optional key
`DEVKIT_TODO_SUPABASE_KEY` resolves to.

```toml
[todo.supabase]
url = "https://abcdefghijklmnop.supabase.co"
doppler_project = "swarm"
```

doppler_config.description: The Doppler config to read it from. Doppler's own default when absent.

doppler_project.description:
Read the key, when the environment lacks it, from this Doppler
project, before the secrets file. Hooks reuse the key Doppler last
gave, kept in devkit's state directory, until it ages out.

root.description:
The database tenant containing this workflow's todos, the one
`[todo.postgres] root` names on machines that connect directly.
Defaults to `devkit`.

url.description:
The project's API URL, `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co`. Read
from `~/.config/devkit/config.toml` (or `$DEVKIT_CONFIG`) alone and
ignored in a project's `devkit.toml`, so a checkout cannot send your
key elsewhere. `DEVKIT_TODO_SUPABASE_URL` overrides it.

TaskConfig.description:
A canned oneshot invoked by name via `devrun task`: either a command
(`run`, optionally scoped to an `app` for cwd + static_env) or a sequence
(`steps`). Exactly one of `run`/`steps` must be set; a sequence task
carries no `app`/`env`. Validated at resolution, not at parse.

```toml
[tasks.api-prod-build]
description = "prod nitro build (node-server preset)"
app = "api-prod"        # run in this app's dir, inherit its static_env
run = ["doppler", "run", "-c", "dev_local",
       "--preserve-env=NITRO_PRESET", "--", "bun", "nitro", "build"]
env = { NITRO_PRESET = "node-server" }

[tasks.commit]
run = ["git", "commit", "-m", "{% if issue is defined %}{{ issue }}: {% endif %}{{ msg }}"]
guard = true            # redirect an agent's own `git commit` here

[tasks.profile-lab-os]
description = "prod api + profiled lab-os, wired together"
steps = [
  { task = "api-prod-build" },
  { up = "api-prod" },
]
```

`msg` is an arg of the `commit` task: no `[templates.variables]` entry
supplies it, so `devrun task commit --arg msg=...` is required.

app.description:
App whose directory the task runs in, inheriting that app's
`static_env`. Omit to run at the repo root.

description.description: One line shown in `devrun task --list` and the session brief.

env.description:
Env vars set for this task, rendered like `run`, layered over the app's
`static_env` and under the CLI's `--env-file` and `--env`. Tasks get no
`url_env` wiring; reference the app through `ports[...]`.

guard.description:
Force the command guard's decision for this task instead of deriving it.
`true` always redirects a matching command to `devrun task <name>`;
`false` never does. Absent derives from whether devkit changes the
process at all.

require_live.description:
Command tasks only: apps whose server must be live in this worktree
when the task executes. Each name must be referenced through
`ports['<app>']` (not `{{ port }}`); an `--env` override of every value
referencing it waives the check and the allocation. References in
`run` cannot be overridden.

required_args.description:
Args this task requires beyond what `[templates.variables]` markings
say, as name to marking. A task entry beats a variable entry, including
relaxing one to `never`. Neither can lower the derived floor: an arg
with no default is required whatever this says. Each name must be an
arg the task reads. A sequence step inherits its task's markings.

run.description:
The command as one argv (program + args), run in the foreground with
its exit code propagated. Every entry is a minijinja template over
`{{ port }}`, `ports['<app>']`, `[templates.variables]`, and `issue`,
`slug`, `branch` from the worktree; any other name read is an arg of
the task, required unless a variable supplies a default. Minijinja's
`default` filter and `is defined` do not make an arg optional. `issue`,
`slug` and `branch` are undefined outside an issue worktree, so a task
run in both guards them with `{% if issue is defined %}`. The program
must be a plain string. A Doppler invocation is refused for `prd` the
same as an app's `launch`. Mutually exclusive with `steps`.

steps.description:
A sequence run in order, stopping at the first failure, each step a
command task or an `up`. Each step re-resolves its ports and gates
immediately before it runs. A sequence sets only `description` and
`steps`, and cannot name another sequence. Mutually exclusive with
`run`.

TaskchampionConfig.description:
Where `[todo] backend = "taskchampion"` keeps its replica and syncs it.
With no `server_dir`, the replica syncs to a server when
`DEVKIT_TODO_SYNC_URL`, `DEVKIT_TODO_SYNC_CLIENT_ID` and
`DEVKIT_TODO_SYNC_SECRET` all resolve, and otherwise stays local.
Replicas discovered through `TASKDATA` or taskrc stay local unless
`data_dir` explicitly selects the replica for devkit sync.

data_dir.description:
The replica's directory. When absent, use `TASKDATA`, then the taskrc's
`data.location`, then `taskchampion` under devkit's todo state
directory. Find taskrc through `TASKRC`, then `~/.taskrc`, then
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/task/taskrc` (`~/.config/task/taskrc` when unset or
empty), following includes. A malformed taskrc or missing include warns
and falls back to devkit's state directory. Sync settings in taskrc are
ignored. Set this explicitly to allow devkit sync for a replica
discovered through `TASKDATA` or taskrc; otherwise devkit only reads
and writes it locally, even when a sync target is configured.

doppler_config.description:
The Doppler config to read them from. Doppler's own default when
absent.

doppler_project.description:
Read the server credentials the environment lacks from this Doppler
project, before the secrets file.

server_dir.description:
Sync to this directory instead of a server. The server credentials
are not read when it is set.

Templates.description:
Config-driven minijinja templates for the issue-lifecycle strings. Each
`None` field falls back to its `DEFAULT_*` constant, which reproduces the
historical hardcoded output. `variables` are user constants merged under
every render context. Rendering is strict: an undefined variable is an
error, so a typo surfaces on the first run.

```toml
[templates]
branch             = "{{ prefix }}{{ issue }}-{{ slug }}"
worktree_dir       = "{{ slug }}"
pr_title           = "{{ issue }}: {{ input }}"
pr_body            = "Closes {{ issue }}.\n\n{{ input }}"
issue_summary_path = "{{ worktree }}/.devkit/issue.md"

[templates.variables]
team = "platform"
```

`issue_summary_path` renders `{{ worktree }}` here, which keeps the summary
inside the worktree where a `[preserve]` pattern can name it; left relative
it is taken from `defaults.worktree_root` instead.

branch.description:
Branch name created by `issue setup`. Context: `prefix`, `issue`,
`slug`, `short_slug`, `apps`. Defaults to `{{ prefix }}{{ slug }}`.

branch_max.description:
Longest branch `issue setup` will render. A derived slug is shortened on
a word boundary to fit. A template whose fixed text already fills this
yields the shortest slug still worth reading rather than an error, since
a git ref has no hard length limit. `short_slug` is not measured by it.
Defaults to 46.

checkout_worktree_dir.description:
Worktree directory name created by `issue pr checkout`. Context:
`pr_number`, `pr_title`, `linear_id`, `linear_title`. Titles are
slugified, and the `linear_*` names are historical: they carry
whichever tracker's id and title resolved, and are empty on the
PR-only path. Defaults to `{{ pr_number }}-{{ pr_title }}`, plus
`_[{{ linear_id }}]` when reached through an issue.

checkout_worktree_dir_max.description:
Longest worktree directory name `issue pr checkout` will render.
`pr_title` and `linear_title` are shortened to fit, splitting the budget
when a template renders both. A template whose fixed text already fills
this is an error. Defaults to 46.

commit_message.description:
Message `devkit commit` records. `subject` is the `--subject`
argument, `body` the `--body` argument, and `coauthors` every
`--coauthor`, `;`-separated. Defaults to the subject, then the body
after a blank line, then a `Co-authored-by` trailer per co-author.

custom.description:
Templates no command sends, rendered by `devkit template render
<name>` for the caller to deliver itself. A built-in template never
takes one's name: `render` looks here first.

issue_body.description:
Body of an issue rendered by `issue render`, created by `issue create`,
or written over an existing issue by `issue edit`. `{{ input }}` is the
`--body` argument and `issue_title` is the rendered title, or the
issue's current title when `issue edit` runs without `--title`. A
`[templates.variables]` entry either rendered template reads, marked
`required`, must be passed as `--arg`; `issue edit` without `--title`
asks only for the ones this template reads.

issue_summary.description:
Body of the file `issue setup --summary` writes when the tracker keeps
no summary of its own; a GitHub issue's non-empty body is written
verbatim instead. Context: `issue`,
`title`, `url`, `description`, `state`, `assignee`, `priority`,
`estimate`, `labels`, `parent`, `project`, `worktree`, `branch`, `slug`,
`prefix`, `apps`. A field the tracker left empty renders as the empty
string, so `{% if parent %}` drops its line.

issue_summary_path.description:
Where `issue setup --summary` writes the issue summary file. A relative
path is taken from `defaults.worktree_root`, so the file sits beside
the worktree and outlives it, and is refused when there is no
`worktree_root`. Context: the `issue_summary` context below. Defaults
to `{{ worktree }}/.devkit/ISSUE_SUMMARY_{{ issue }}.md`: inside the
worktree, or the checkout `issue setup --here` binds, where it stays
untracked and goes when `issue end` removes the worktree.

issue_title.description:
Title of an issue rendered by `issue render`, created by `issue
create`, or written by `issue edit --title`. `{{ input }}` is the
`--title` argument; the rendered title must not be empty. `issue edit`
without `--title` keeps the issue's title and does not render this.

pr_body.description:
Body of a PR rendered by `issue pr render` or opened by `issue pr
create`. `{{ input }}` is the `--pr-body` argument. `issue pr create`
renders it only when it opens a PR, not when it reuses an open one.

pr_title.description:
Title of a PR rendered by `issue pr render` or opened by `issue pr
create`. `{{ input }}` is the `--pr-title` argument; the rendered title
must not be empty.

review_finish.description:
Slack message sent by `issue review finish`. Same context as
`review_request`, plus `author`.

review_request.description:
Slack message sent by `issue review request`. Rendered once per
recipient with `name`, `slack_id` (empty for a channel), `pr_url`,
`pr_title` (the PR's own title from GitHub), `input`, and `branch`,
`issue`, `slug`, `apps` from the worktree's `.devkit/issue.toml`.

variables.description:
Constants available to every template above. A context field of the same
name wins, and `--arg key=value` overrides either. An entry may instead
be a table carrying a `default`, a `required` marking and a
`description` of what to pass. `role` and `sha` are reserved and
rejected here.

worktree_dir.description:
Worktree directory name created by `issue setup`, relative to
`defaults.worktree_root`. Same context as `branch`; defaults to
`{{ slug }}`.

worktree_dir_max.description:
Longest worktree directory name `issue setup` will render from
`{{ short_slug }}`. A template whose fixed text already fills this is an
error: a limit on a filesystem path that does not hold is worse than a
setup that stops. Has no effect on a `worktree_dir` that does not render
`{{ short_slug }}`. Defaults to 24.

TodoConfig.description:
Where agent todo lists are kept.

```toml
[todo]
backend = "taskchampion"
hold_stop = "always"

[todo.taskchampion]
data_dir = "/var/devkit/todo"
server_dir = "/mnt/shared/todo-sync"
doppler_project = "devkit"
doppler_config = "dev"

[todo.postgres]
root = "agents"
doppler_project = "swarm"
doppler_config = "agents"
ca_file = "~/.config/devkit/supabase-ca.crt"

[todo.supabase]
url = "https://abcdefghijklmnop.supabase.co"
root = "agents"
```

backend.description:
Which store keeps the todos. `builtin` is a JSON file in devkit's
state directory. `taskchampion` keeps bare project nodes in an embedded
replica and can sync it to a directory or server. `postgres` keeps
them in a shared database under `todo.postgres.root`, with its activity
log. `supabase` reaches that database's todos and activity log over a
Supabase project's HTTPS Data API, for a machine that can make HTTP
requests but not open a Postgres connection.
`DEVKIT_TODO_BACKEND` overrides it with the same spellings.

hold_stop.description:
Whose stop a stop hook refuses while the agent has open todos: its
own claims on any node and pending todos when its role holds them.
`always` holds every agent, `subagents` only sub-agents, and `never`
none; `true` and `false` mean `always` and `never`. One reminder per
unchanged list; stopping again goes through. A Claude Code main
agent's stop while its background tasks or session crons are in
flight is never refused.
`DEVKIT_TODO_HOLD_STOP` overrides it with the same spellings, and
`devkit todo hold` overrides both for one session.

roles.description:
Workflow roles. `main` and `subagent` always exist; a layer may
redefine them or add roles for its own workflow.

scopes.description:
Named node templates and their parents. Defaults are extended or
overridden key by key by each config layer.

TrackerConfig.description:
The `[tracker]` table.

```toml
[tracker]
kind = "github"
```

Naming the kind is what stops a `LINEAR_API_KEY` exported machine-wide from
resolving Linear for a project that does not use it.

Every tracker question goes through the resolved tracker: `issue setup`'s
slug and summary, `issue pr checkout`'s bare-number disambiguation,
`issue dashboard`'s timeline, and the ISSUE column of `issue prs`.

kind.description:
Force a tracker instead of detecting one. Detection also decides when
no config resolves: outside any devkit project, or when the config
fails to load. Every `issue` command and the `issue.status` MCP action
read it. `github` authenticates through `gh auth login`, `GH_TOKEN` or
`GITHUB_TOKEN`; under it a bare number is a PR, since issues and PRs
share one numbering, and with no resolvable `[github] issues_repo` the
project runs with no tracker. `none` declares no issue states, so a
merged PR and a clean tree finish a worktree. Detection that finds
nothing is different: it holds that verdict open, because `issue end`
deletes branches. `devkit doctor`'s `tracker` row shows which tracker
resolved and why.

TrackerKind.description:
Which issue tracker a project uses. Absent means detect: a resolvable
`LINEAR_API_KEY`, then a GitHub `origin` remote, then no tracker.

description.description:
What to pass for this arg, shown beside it where devkit asks for
it: a missing-arg error (`issue pr create` and `issue review`
included), a command-guard redirect to a task that reads it,
`devkit config tasks <name>` and `devkit config variables`.
Explain an arg here rather than in a guard rule's `reason`.

required.description:
`None` is a marking the author did not write, which is not the same
as one written as `never`: an unmarked valueless entry is required
by the derived rule, while `required = "never"` on the same entry
asks to relax that and is refused at load.

VariableDecl.description:
One `[templates.variables]` entry: a bare string, or a table carrying a
`default`, a `required` marking and a `description`.

`deny_unknown_fields` for the reason `RunAction` documents: under untagged
matching a misspelled key beside a well-formed pair deserializes silently,
and the author sees no diagnostic while their guard does nothing.

```toml
[templates.variables]
team = "platform"                              # a constant, never required
msg = { default = "wip", required = "agents" } # defaulted, but agents must pass it
ticket = { required = "always" }               # declared, no default, always required
body = { default = "", description = "why the change was made, if the subject does not say" }
```

`default` is the fallback used when nothing else supplies the name, which
is what these entries have always been: `template::render` merges them
underneath the context, and `--arg` overwrites them. Note that minijinja's
own `default` filter is a different thing and does not affect whether an
arg is required.

description: Configuration for the devkit CLIs (devrun, portm, issue, lockm, docm, devkit).

apps.description:
One table per runnable app, keyed by the app id passed to
`issue setup --apps` and `devrun up`.

brief.description: Which sections `devkit brief` emits at session start.

config.description: Layer-stack control: `root = true` stops the upward walk here.

context.description:
Files injected into an agent's context, each gated by its own
condition.

daemon.description:
The `devkitd` supervisor: autostart gate, crash-loop budget, and the
memory and health policies applied to supervised servers.

forge.description:
Which forge holds this project's pull requests. Detected when the table
is absent.

github.description:
Which GitHub repository backs the GitHub tracker's issues, and which
Projects v2 project holds their status.

hooks.description:
Commands devkit runs when a lifecycle event fires, keyed
`{before,after}_<event>`.

issue.description:
What devkit does to an issue's tracker status when it acts on that
issue.

linear.description: Linear lookups that cost an extra API round trip.

mcp.description: The `devkit-mcp` server the agent plugins start.

parallelism.description:
Width of the shared worker pool. Machine tuning; carries no project
convention, so a config may hold it alone.

people.description:
Reviewer/recipient aliases, keyed by the short name passed to
`issue review --to`.

preserve.description:
Files copied out of an issue worktree before `issue end` removes it,
keyed by the name that labels the entry's progress step and its
warnings.

rules.description:
Rule injection settings: enablement, severity floor, and the per-event
size budget.

tasks.description: Canned oneshot commands, keyed by the name passed to `devrun task`.

templates.description:
Minijinja templates for the strings `issue setup` and `issue review`
generate — branch names, worktree directories, PR fields, Slack bodies.

todo.description: Where `devkit todo` and the todo hooks keep agent todo lists.

tracker.description: Which issue tracker backs `issue`. Detected when the table is absent.

title: devkit.toml
